messages:
maria: Heads up — opened a PR to split the aws provider out of our core infra module and pin provider versions at the repo root. Need quick eyes on migration strategy before I merge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/487

devin: Can you paste the current provider blocks and the new ones you put in the PR? also which Terraform version + backend?

maria: TF v1.5.6, backend = s3 (redwood-terraform-state). Current modules had provider blocks like this inside modules/core/providers.tf: 
```terraform
provider "aws" {
  region = var.region
  version = "~> 4.45"
}
```
I moved provider blocks to the root (root main.tf) and tightened to `~> 4.50`. Also changed a few modules to accept an injected provider alias instead of creating their own. My worry: provider address changes in state and lockfile churn causing CI plan to fail.

alok: Moving provider blocks is fine but watch provider addresses. If you change from module-local provider to root provider, TF will see provider addresses as different (e.g., registry.terraform.io/-/aws -> registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws or module path differences). You likely need either:
- keep compatibility by adding provider aliases in root and passing them into modules for one release cycle, or
- run `terraform state replace-provider` to map old provider addresses to new ones before applying.

Example `state replace-provider` snippet: 
```bash
# from the old module-scoped provider to the root-managed one
terraform state replace-provider 'registry.terraform.io/-/aws' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws'
```
(verify the exact address via `terraform providers` / state list first)

sam: Also check .terraform.lock.hcl — running `terraform init -upgrade` will update the lockfile. CI plan checks will fail if the lockfile in the PR doesn't match what's generated by the runner. If CI runs on linux amd64 but you generated lockfile for darwin, you'll get diffs. Use `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` if needed.

infra-bot: CI: terraform/plan (infra) — pipeline #12345 failed on PR #487 — changed provider checks. Full logs: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/12345/logs (plan shows provider address changes but no resource replacements yet) :warning:

devin: Important: provider address changes alone can be noisy but benign if you remap. Confirm plan does not show any `-/+` or `delete` for real resources. If it does, do not merge. Also check any data "aws_iam_policy_document" or data sources that might depend on provider aliases (they can be sensitive).

olivia: For safety, do a two-step rollout: merge the module refactor with compatibility aliases that keep old provider addresses, run a non-destructive plan in prod (or in a staging workspace that mirrors prod), then run a separate PR that does the state replace + lockfile update and bump module version. That minimizes risk and gives us a rollback point. Also update our internal module registry entry (we version modules semver-like, please create a new patch version).

maria: Good call. My plan update:
1) revert the PR to include provider alias fallbacks and keep module inputs compatible.
2) run `terraform init -upgrade -backend-config=...` in a staging workspace to regenerate lockfile for linux_amd64.
3) run `terraform state replace-provider` in a controlled maintenance window with ops on call.
4) open a follow-up PR to remove compatibility aliases and finalize provider move.

devin: Sounds good. One more check — secrets wiring: do any modules take a KMS key via variable that you changed? If you change variable names or module interface, state needs to keep the same references.

maria: No variable renames. KMS key ARN was passed through same var `kms_key_arn`. I did add an optional `provider_alias` input to the module.

alok: If you add `provider_alias` keep it optional and default to `null` so we don't force consumers to change immediately. Also run `terraform state list | grep module.core` and `terraform show -json plan.out | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions != ["no-op"])'` locally to sanity check.

sam: I'll help coordinate the maintenance window and run the state replace with you, @maria. Also will pin the CI runner platforms so lockfile generation matches.

maria: Thanks all — I'll update the PR with aliases and add a migration script with the `state replace-provider` commands and a short runbook. Will @mention infra-oncall before doing the state change. :thumbsup:

olivia: Thanks — please tag me on the module version bump so I can publish the new registry entry. :eyes:

infra-bot: Note: remember to update docs/terraform/README.md about provider pinning and lockfile generation.

maria: Will do — closing for now, will re-open PR once I push the alias-compatible changes.
